_meta.purpose: Real, sourced dimensions of a canonical example temple for each architecture form. The procedural 3D models on temple-forms.html are built to THESE proportions (base:height ratios, counts of wheels/columns/storeys), so the shapes are true to life, not invented. Figures are documented measurements, not LiDAR point clouds — where a figure is an estimate (e.g. a collapsed tower) it is flagged.
_meta.note: All heights in metres. 'real_scan' links a genuine open 3D capture where one exists; null where the best available is AI-generated or non-free.

nagara.notes: Nagara curvilinear shikhara clustered with 84 miniature towers (Mount Kailasa). ASI: 30.5 m long ≈ 30.5 m high, 20 m wide, on a ~3 m platform.

dravidian.notes: Tallest vimana of its age: a 13-storey stone pyramid ~66 m over the sanctum, octagonal griva + monolithic ~80-tonne capstone. Its gopurams are lower than the vimana here (unusual); most Dravidian temples have gopurams taller than the vimana.
dravidian.source: ASI; UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brihadeeswarar_Temple

stupa.notes: Solid hemispherical anda 36.6 m across, 16.46 m high (dome only). Squared harmika + triple chhatra on the axis; four toranas at the cardinal points.

jain.notes: Light marble; 1,444 unique pillars, 29 pillared halls, 80 domes over a ~48,000 sq ft base. Four doorways to a four-faced Adinatha — a symmetrical chaumukha plan.

kashmiri.notes: Square shrine on a high plinth inside a colonnaded courtyard of ~84 fluted columns; the Kashmiri signature is the steep PEAKED (pyramidal) roof and trefoil arches. Ruined; proportions from surviving plan.

sun_temple.notes: Chariot of Surya: 24 wheels (12 pairs = months, each an 8-spoke sundial) drawn by 7 horses (7 days / metres of prosody). Surviving jagamohana 30 m sq × ~30 m; the ~70 m deul collapsed.

egyptian.notes: Great Hypostyle Hall: 134 massive columns (central 12 ~21 m tall) with papyrus/lotus capitals; twin battered pylons front the axis; obelisks mark the sun/Nile alignment.

greek.notes: Peripteral Doric: 8×17 columns on a 30.9×69.5 m stylobate, ~10.4 m columns, ~13.7 m to the ridge, pervasive 4:9 proportion, curved stylobate + column entasis (optical correction).
greek.real_scan_credit: Parthenon — Acropolis, Athens, by Nick G. Gizelis (@aumakua), drone photogrammetry, CC-BY

mesoamerican.notes: Stepped pyramid ~225 m per side, ~65 m high today (~71–75 m originally with its lost summit temple), 5 tiers, 248-step central stair. A stage for ritual, over a cave.

ziggurat.notes: Mud-brick step pyramid, base 64×45 m, three receding terraces, triple converging stairway to the moon-god Nanna's shrine. Only the lower terraces survive; 30 m height is an estimate.

andean.example: Machu Picchu (Temple of the Sun / Intihuatana)
andean.notes: Dry-stone polygonal masonry (no mortar), ~700 agricultural terraces at 2,430 m, trapezoidal doors/windows, curved Temple of the Sun aligned to the June solstice. Chavín de Huántar gives the definitive dark interior gallery + Lánzon.

moai.notes: The largest ahu: 15 moai in a row facing inland over the village. Tallest re-erected moai ~10 m; heaviest ~86 t. ~900 moai island-wide.

ethiopian.example: Bete Giyorgis (Church of St George), Lalibela
ethiopian.notes: A cruciform church cut ~12 m DOWN into living volcanic rock — one continuous stone, no joints, standing in a sunken pit reached by trenches. One of Lalibela's 11 rock churches.

petra.notes: A ~39 m tall, ~25 m wide classical facade carved back INTO the rose-red cliff, with a broken pediment framing a central round tholos crowned by an urn; a modest chamber behind.

elephanta.notes: A pillared hall ~39 m across excavated into basalt; pillars are left standing, not placed. The back wall carries the ~5.5 m three-headed Trimurti Shiva — sculpture and structure are one stone.

megalithic_circle.notes: Outer ring ~33 m across of ~30 upright sarsens capped by curved lintels (mortise-and-tenon), an inner horseshoe of 5 giant trilithons on the midsummer-sunrise / midwinter-sunset axis.
